Letter dated June 19, 1972, from Chairman, Board of Trustees, Environmental Defense Fund.
Comment: The letter objects to use of the term, "productive levels" used in paragraph 3 on the Summary Page. The sentence in question reads, "Restrict man's economic and cultural use of endangered species until these species are restored to productive levels."
Response: We agree that the sentence is unclear as to the point at which a restored endangered species population may be used for consumptive purposes by man. The statement has been changed to provide that the population must have reached the point where numbers excess to the capacity of available and restored habitat are produced on a sustained annual basis.
Regarding the fifth paragraph under the "Impacts" section of the draft statement, EDF objects to wording about the harvest of whales. In the new draft the "Impacts" section has been revised, and no reference is made to restoration of whales.
<u>Comment</u>: EDF points out that the last paragraph in the Mitigating Measures section is not clear in its meaning.
Response: The entire section has been revised to make it clearer.
Comment: Under the "Adverse Effects" section, EDF points out that in paragraph one cultural benefits will not be lost because Aleuts, Eskimos and American Indians are specifically excepted from provisions of the proposed legislation. They go on to disagree with paragraph three which lists. as adverse the restriction or elimination of man's activities in habitat occupied by endangered species.
